newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard says court agrees ink jet d.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard says court agrees ink jet d.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said Thursday that a court accepted the company's proposal for revising the product illustration on the packages of two of its black inkjet cartridges.

At the same time, the court rebuffed all remedies sought by Nu-kote International and required that Nu-kote post a $75,000 bond against any harm the packaging change might cause Hewlett-Packard, a news release issued by the company said.
The company revised its estimate of the cost of modifying the cartridge illustration on the packaging down from between $3 million and $6 million to under half a million dollars.
The hearing followed a July 11 ruling by Judge James Ware of U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on an injunction motion made by Nu-kote, the release said.

In that ruling, Judge Ware denied Nu-kote's request that Hewlett-Packard be required to halt conversion of its manufacturing lines to a new bottom-ink-fill format design for its 51626A and 51629A black inkjet cartridges, the news release said.
The judge ruled that Hewlett-Packard should change the illustration of the cartridge on the packaging for the older top-ink-fill format design of the 26A and 29A cartridges, the release said.

Nu-Kote, which markets ink that can be injected into older-style HP cartridges, had asked the court to stop HP from making a new design of the popular cartridges because a so-called top ink-fill hole was removed.

Nu-Kote had argued that Hewlett-Packard was unfairly restricting competition by eliminating the hole, which Nu-kote's products have utilized to enable customers to inject fresh ink into the cartridges.
